message.content:
The earliest non‑biblical references to Jesus come from Roman and Jewish writers who lived within a few decades of his death.

| Author | Work | Date | Reference |
|--------|------|------|-----------|
| **Flavius Josephus** | *Antiquities of the Jews* (Book 18, Chapter 3) | c. 93–94 CE | “...the wise man was called Jesus…” |
| **Tacitus** | *Annals* (Book 15, Chapter 44) | c. 116 CE | “Christus, the founder of the name, was executed …” |
| **Pliny the Younger** | Letter to Emperor Trajan (Letter 10.96) | c. 112 CE | “They worship Christ as a god.” |

Josephus’s passage is the earliest surviving mention; it appears in a section written about 20–30 years after Jesus’s crucifixion. Tacitus’s account follows a few decades later but is considered more reliable because he was a contemporary historian with access to official records. These references are widely accepted by scholars as evidence that Jesus existed historically.

According to historians, earliest references include Josephus (Antiquities 18.3) and Tacitus (Annals 15.44). Also maybe Pliny the Younger (letters). But earliest is Josephus, around AD 93-94.
